shortAnswer: Otterly.ai is a solid, affordable AI-search monitor, but the $29 Lite plan tracks only ~15 prompts and the next tier jumps to $189/mo, with Gemini, Google AI Mode and Claude as paid add-ons. If you want a free, instant way to see how AI engines talk about your brand, AEOeye runs a blind multi-engine audit at no cost. intro:
Otterly.ai earned its reputation as the budget-friendly on-ramp to AI search visibility — a 4.8 G2 rating and a 2025 Gartner Cool Vendor nod back that up. It tracks whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Copilot mention your brand and cite your site, with daily monitoring and 50+ country coverage.

But people still shop for alternatives, usually for three reasons: the pricing jumps hard from the entry tier, the marquee AI engines cost extra as add-ons, and the tool tells you where you stand without telling you what to do next. Below we lay out those gaps fairly, then compare the best alternatives — starting with a free, instant option and including strong paid platforms for teams that need more depth.

sections.heading: Why people look for Otterly.ai alternatives
sections.body:
Otterly is a capable monitoring tool, and for solo marketers it's often enough. The friction shows up when you try to scale it into a real program, or when you expect the data to translate directly into action. Three themes come up repeatedly in reviews and on Reddit.

None of these make Otterly a bad tool — it's well-built and fairly priced for what it includes. They're just the predictable points where teams start comparing it against other options. The sections below break each one down with the specifics, so you can judge whether they actually matter for your situation or whether Otterly's entry tier covers you fine.

sections.heading: 1. The jump from entry to mid-tier pricing is steep
sections.body:
Otterly's $29 Lite plan is genuinely cheap, but it only covers about 15 tracked prompts. Most reviewers consider that too few to run a meaningful monitoring program — a single product line with a handful of buyer questions and a few competitor comparisons can exhaust it quickly.

The problem is what comes next. There's nothing between Lite and Standard at $189/month (100 prompts) — roughly a 6x jump with no middle step. Teams that outgrow 15 prompts have no gentle upgrade path; they leap straight to $189. And if 100 prompts isn't enough, extra 100-prompt packs run about $99/month each on the paid tiers, so costs compound fast.

For a freelancer tracking one brand, Lite may be fine indefinitely. For an agency or a growing in-house team, the pricing curve gets uncomfortable right at the point where AI visibility monitoring starts paying off.

sections.heading: 2. Key AI engines cost extra as add-ons
sections.body:
Otterly's headline is multi-engine monitoring, and the base plans do include four real engines: ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Copilot. That's a solid core.

The nuance is what's not included. Gemini, Google AI Mode and Claude are paid add-ons, priced from about $9 to $149+/month each depending on your tier. Google AI Mode in particular is becoming a primary AI-search surface inside Google, so leaving it behind an add-on means the lowest tiers don't see a fast-growing slice of the picture by default.

The practical effect: a $189/month Standard plan can realistically climb past $300 once you bolt on the engines you actually want covered. The multi-engine story is real, but it becomes fully true only after you pay for it. If complete cross-engine coverage out of the box matters to you, that's worth pricing carefully before committing.

sections.heading: 3. It monitors, but doesn't tell you what to do
sections.body:
This is the most consistent critique. Otterly shows you where you stand — which prompts mention you, which competitors win, where you're invisible — but it stops short of telling you how to change it. One Reddit user put it bluntly: it 'tracks the source but gives zero actionable strategy on how to restructure content to get cited.'

Otterly does offer a GEO Audit, but reviewers describe it as flagging issues without step-by-step fixes — you're expected to know how to implement the recommendations or hire someone who does. There's no built-in content writer and no guided path from 'I'm missing from these prompts' to 'here's the content that changes that.'

It also doesn't connect AI mentions to traffic or conversions, so the loop back to revenue stays open. You get a clear diagnosis; the treatment plan is on you. For teams that want monitoring plus direction, this gap is the main reason to look elsewhere.

sections.heading: The best Otterly.ai alternatives in 2026
sections.body:
There's no single 'best' replacement — the right pick depends on whether you want a free instant check, a budget monitor, a mid-market analytics platform, or enterprise-grade depth. Here are the alternatives worth a look, described honestly.

**AEOeye — free, instant, multi-engine audit.** AEOeye runs a free AI visibility audit on the spot: it asks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini the questions real buyers ask, then shows whether each engine recommends your brand, where you rank, and which competitors win. No trial-card, no sales call, no contract — you see results in minutes. The trade-off is honest: AEOeye is newer and lighter on enterprise analytics and long-run historical dashboards than incumbents like Profound, and its deepest multi-engine querying ramps up with usage. It's the best way to see where you stand today before paying for an ongoing program — and a genuine no-cost starting point Otterly doesn't offer (Otterly has only a 14-day trial).

**Otterly.ai — the budget monitor (staying on it).** If your needs fit ~15 prompts or you can live at the $189 tier, Otterly is well-rated, easy to use, and now ships an MCP server, public API and a Claude Skill. A fair default for solo marketers and SMBs.

**Peec AI — mid-market analytics.** Peec starts around €75–€89/month (≈25 prompts) and scales to ~€169/month for 100, with strong competitor-benchmarking and clean dashboards. A natural step up from Otterly without enterprise pricing, and no annual lock-in on lower tiers.

**Profound — enterprise depth.** Self-serve Lite starts around $499/month, with custom enterprise contracts. It tracks the broadest engine set (up to ~10, including Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek and Meta AI), is SOC-2 Type II certified, and serves 700+ enterprise customers. Overkill for small teams; the leader for large ones.

**Nightwatch — AI plus traditional SEO.** Starting around $32/month, Nightwatch combines LLM monitoring with classic rank tracking and citation-level sentiment, so you consolidate AI and traditional SEO in one tool. Best if you don't want a separate platform for each.

faqs.q: Is there a free alternative to Otterly.ai?
faqs.a: Yes. Otterly offers only a 14-day free trial, not a free-forever plan. AEOeye runs a free, instant AI visibility audit — it queries ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini with real buyer questions and shows whether they recommend your brand, where you rank, and which competitors win — with no card, sales call, or contract. It's the fastest way to see where you stand before paying for ongoing monitoring.

faqs.q: Why is Otterly.ai more expensive than its $29 sticker price suggests?
faqs.a: The $29 Lite plan covers only about 15 prompts. The next tier is $189/month (100 prompts) with nothing in between, and extra 100-prompt packs run ~$99/month. On top of that, Gemini, Google AI Mode and Claude are paid add-ons ($9–$149+/month each), so full multi-engine coverage on a $189 plan can realistically exceed $300/month.

faqs.q: Which Otterly alternative is best for enterprises?
faqs.a: Profound is the strongest enterprise option in 2026. Self-serve starts around $499/month, it tracks the broadest engine set (up to ~10, including Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek and Meta AI), is SOC-2 Type II certified, and serves 700+ enterprise customers. It's more than small teams need, but it's built for scale and depth.

faqs.q: Does Otterly.ai tell you how to improve your AI visibility?
faqs.a: Mostly no. Otterly is monitoring-first: it shows which prompts mention you, where competitors win, and where you're invisible. Its GEO Audit flags issues but, per reviewers, doesn't give step-by-step fixes, and it doesn't tie AI mentions to traffic or conversions. If you want diagnosis plus direction, that gap is the main reason people look at alternatives.

faqs.q: What engines does AEOeye check that Otterly charges extra for?
faqs.a: AEOeye's audit covers ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI, Claude and Gemini together at no cost. On Otterly, Gemini, Google AI Mode and Claude sit behind paid add-ons rather than the base plans, so the same breadth costs more there. Be aware AEOeye is newer and lighter on long-run historical dashboards than incumbents — it's best for an instant, blind snapshot of where you stand.
